basics.name: Robert Schäfer
basics.label: Full Stack Engineer
basics.summary: Hi, my name is Robert, full-stack engineer, speaker and mentor. I started computer science in 2009 and have been developing full-stack applications since 2012. The technologies I'm most familiar with right now are: VueJS, TailwindCSS, NuxtJS, GraphQL, Apollo, NodeJS, Ruby on Rails, Neo4J, Ansible, Serverless, Docker and Kubernetes. I speak at tech meetups and advocate free and open source software. I am also a programming mentor and teach full-stack development courses at university. At work, I value the transfer of knowledge within the team and am often responsible for training new co-workers. I prefer remote work and am open to freelance work and contracts. My current interests are modern Node.js backends (Nest.js), infrastructure as code (Terraform), cross-platform development (React Native, Flutter) and modern compiled languages (Golang, Rust).

projects.description: With this platform for remotely controlling telescopes through the  astrophotography software NINA, deep-sky imaging gets accessible without  owning expensive hardware or the expertise to operate it. Users select  an astronomical target and book observation time; the application sends  imaging sequences to NINA via Tailscale, which executes them overnight  and delivers the results. The core challenge is turning a Windows-only,  inherently interactive application into a fully autonomous pipeline.

This SvelteKit application for AI-assisted interviews and editorial  publishing replaces brittle infrastructure spread across Airtable,  Voiceflow, and additional custom services with a single serverless  application. Using the built-in workflows of ElevenLabs AI Agents  significantly reduces maintenance overhead and complexity while  improving the phone agent's response time by several seconds, which is  crucial for a good user experience.

Migrated assets from a Kubernetes volume to S3-compatible object storage  to reduce deployment complexity and cost. Rebuilt the infrastructure  with Terraform and sops, and moved from a managed Kubernetes cluster on  Digital Ocean to a self-hosted Kubernetes cluster on Hetzner, cutting  monthly costs by 80%.

For this free and open-source social platform for entrepreneurs, the  delivery and infrastructure architecture was fundamentally reworked  after deployments had previously been performed manually via a remote  desktop on the target server, regularly causing downtime. Moving the  project to a self-managed Kubernetes setup on Hetzner with Terraform  gave every developer production-like test environments for their own  branches while keeping operating costs extremely low at under 20 euros  per month.
